title: Pub Visibility
story: Your `math_utils` module has a clever `fast_sqrt` function that users should use, and an internal `babylonian_step` helper that they should NEVER call directly. How do you expose the first and hide the second? With `pub` — the visibility keyword that draws the line between public API and internal implementation.
why: Visibility control is essential for building libraries — public items form the stable API contract, while private internals can change freely without breaking callers.
analogy: `pub` vs private is like a restaurant kitchen — the dining room (public API) is where customers interact: they see the menu (pub functions). The kitchen (private internals) is off-limits: customers can't walk in and start cooking. The chef (module author) can reorganize the kitchen without affecting the dining experience.
try_it: Add a `pub` function `reset_password` that calls the private `hash_password`. Then try calling `auth.hash_password("test")` from main — does it compile? (No! Private means private.) Now add a second public function that internally uses `hash_password` — notice how you changed the internal helper without affecting the public API.
tips: Everything is private unless marked `pub` — when in doubt, keep it private; you can always make it public later
Your public API is a commitment — once people depend on a `pub` function, removing it breaks their code
Private helpers can change freely — rename, refactor, delete them without worrying about external callers
common_mistakes: Making everything pub 'just in case' — you can't un-publish something later without breaking users
Forgetting `pub` on functions users need — the error message when calling a private function tells you exactly what's wrong
Marking types as pub but forgetting to mark their methods — a pub type with private methods is a locked door
